name: beautifulsoup4

family: Beautiful Soup bs4 tree builder over lxml.etree XMLParser over libxml2 2.15.4 XML parser
family_note: Not an independent XML tokenizer. It shares the lxml/libxml2 parser family with projects/xml/python/lxml (same lxml 6.1.3 and libxml2 2.15.4 pins), differing in recover=True, the push-feed path and bs4's tree construction.
parser_options_caveat: bs4 creates lxml.etree.XMLParser(target=builder, recover=True, huge_tree=False, encoding=<EncodingDetector guess>); recover=True makes this path lenient where projects/xml/python/lxml uses recover=False. No malformed-input behavior was tested.

name: defusedxml
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/defusedxml/0.7.1/json (License: PSFL; classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: Python Software Foundation License'); the wheel's defusedxml-0.7.1.dist-info/LICENSE and the sdist LICENSE are byte-identical (sha256 b80ce9da8c42a1f91079627fbbe2bf27210ae108a0ffe5f077d5b08e076c24c8, PSF License Agreement for Python 2.7). Source modules say 'Licensed to PSF under a Contributor Agreement.'
input_api: defusedxml.ElementTree.parse(BytesIO(local XML bytes)) with default forbid_dtd=False, forbid_entities=True, forbid_external=True; getroot(); Element.tag, attrib, text and tail
documentation_evidence: The 0.7.1 README (shipped in the sdist) shows 'from defusedxml.ElementTree import parse; et = parse(xmlfile)' as the drop-in replacement for xml.etree.ElementTree.parse and lists parse(), iterparse(), fromstring() and XMLParser for defusedxml.ElementTree, with the forbid_dtd/forbid_entities/forbid_external keyword arguments and their defaults.

dependencies.role: C XML parser loaded by CPython pyexpat, built from source

scope: Valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 local byte streams without DOCTYPE through defusedxml.ElementTree.parse: namespace-expanded element tags ({uri}local) in document order, namespace-expanded attribute names and values in source order, stripped text and tail data (CDATA included), tree depth, the root tag, and the namespace URIs carried by expanded element and attribute names. ElementTree resolves namespaces but keeps no xmlns declarations or prefixes, and its default TreeBuilder drops comments and processing instructions.
family: defusedxml guarded ElementTree facade over CPython xml.etree.ElementTree XMLParser/pyexpat over Expat 2.10.0
family_note: Not an independent XML engine. defusedxml.ElementTree.parse() creates DefusedXMLParser, a subclass of CPython's pure-Python xml.etree.ElementTree.XMLParser (defusedxml re-imports ElementTree.py with the _elementtree accelerator blocked), whose only additions are DTD/entity/external-reference guard handlers installed on pyexpat; the stdlib ElementTree.parse feeds it, Expat tokenizes and checks well-formedness, ElementTree.py's XMLParser callbacks expand names, and the C _elementtree TreeBuilder builds the tree. It shares the Expat family with xmltodict, untangle (which uses defusedxml's SAX module) and the standard xml.etree.ElementTree path (same Expat 2.10.0 pin).
namespace_caveat: ElementTree discards xmlns declarations, so the summary has no namespace_declarations count and its namespaces field lists the URIs in expanded names. On both controls this equals the declared non-empty URIs; the comparison with the independent lxml/libxml2 oracle drops only the declaration count.
parser_options_caveat: defusedxml.ElementTree.parse defaults are forbid_dtd=False, forbid_entities=True, forbid_external=True: the guards replace pyexpat's EntityDeclHandler, UnparsedEntityDeclHandler and ExternalEntityRefHandler but are never called on these DOCTYPE-free controls. No DTD, entity, security or malformed-input behavior was tested.

verification_note: Shared Expat family, not an independent XML engine: defusedxml.ElementTree.parse() builds DefusedXMLParser, a subclass of CPython's pure-Python xml.etree.ElementTree.XMLParser (defusedxml re-imports ElementTree.py with the _elementtree accelerator blocked), whose own additions are guard handlers installed on pyexpat for entity declarations, unparsed entity declarations and external entity references; stdlib ElementTree.parse feeds the stream, Expat 2.10.0 tokenizes and checks well-formedness, ElementTree.py's XMLParser callbacks expand namespace names, and the C _elementtree TreeBuilder builds the tree. The pinned image asserts the pure-Python base class, the C TreeBuilder target, the installed guards and pyexpat.EXPAT_VERSION. ElementTree resolves namespaces ({uri}local tags and attribute names) but keeps no xmlns declarations or prefixes, so the summary omits the lxml path's namespace_declarations count and lists the URIs carried by expanded names. Both shared valid namespace controls match an independent namespace-aware lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 oracle, run in the verified lxml image, on every remaining field; the oracle's summary equals the lxml path's without the declaration count, and its expanded-name URIs equal its declared non-empty URIs on both controls. The first control executes 20 defusedxml lines (13 in defusedxml/ElementTree.py, 7 in common.py), 71 CPython xml/etree/ElementTree.py driver lines and 2,560 Expat lines (1,808 in xmlparse.c); the second executes 20, 79 and 2,806 (1,894). The AFL++ bridge maps the parse call's defusedxml/ElementTree.py lines plus Expat regions and branches: five identical runs of each control yield identical features, and the second control changes 840 Expat features, 8 ElementTree.py lines and 800 AFL++ tuple IDs. defusedxml's own 20 lines (guard installation and the parse factory) are identical on both controls; they are kept as features because the guard callbacks would run only on DTD entity or external-reference input, which was not tested. Input dependence on these controls comes from Expat and the ElementTree driver. PYTHONHASHSEED=1 is fixed because pyexpat passes CPython's hash secret to XML_SetHashSalt and a zero seed makes Expat draw a random salt. CPython's ElementTree.py, pyexpat and _elementtree are Ubuntu's distribution build; only Expat is source-built, and the C TreeBuilder is not covered. The controls do not establish DTD, entity, security, non-UTF-8, XML 1.1 or malformed-input behavior; comments and processing instructions are dropped by the default TreeBuilder. name: xmlschema
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/xmlschema/4.3.2/json (License-Expression: MIT); the wheel's xmlschema-4.3.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE and the sdist LICENSE are byte-identical (sha256 de71695b2db6819ee4478ef39f5f202aab9f0c8750168c2986467ea8e5fa2997, MIT License, SISSA). Source modules say 'distributed under the terms of the MIT License'.
input_api: xmlschema.XMLResource(BytesIO(local XML bytes)) with default options (defuse='remote', lazy=False, iterparse=xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse); XMLResource.root (Element.tag, attrib, text and tail) and XMLResource.get_xmlns(element) for each element's own xmlns declarations
documentation_evidence: The stable API page (titled 'xmlschema 4.3.2 documentation' on 2026-11-17; source doc/api.rst at https://github.com/sissaschool/xmlschema/blob/v4.3.2/doc/api.rst) documents xmlschema.XMLResource(source, ...) where source is 'a string containing the XML document or file path or a URL or a file like object or an ElementTree or an Element', with root, iter() and get_namespaces(); its iterparse parameter defaults to ElementTree.iterparse. The usage guide (doc/usage.rst in the sdist) says schema and instance processing are based on XMLResource and that namespace mapping is supported by XMLResource internals.

dependencies.role: xmlschema's only runtime dependency (Requires-Dist elementpath<6.0.0,>=5.1.3); imported but not executed by the XMLResource parse call on these controls
C XML parser loaded by CPython pyexpat, built from source

scope: Valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 local byte streams without DOCTYPE through xmlschema.XMLResource: namespace-expanded element tags ({uri}local) in document order, namespace-expanded attribute names and values in source order, stripped text and tail data (CDATA included), tree depth, the root tag, the number of xmlns declarations xmlschema records per element (including the xmlns="" undeclaration), and the non-empty declared namespace URIs. The tree comes from CPython's TreeBuilder, which keeps no comments or processing instructions; xmlschema sees those iterparse events but does not store them.
family: xmlschema XMLResource namespace-tracking loader over CPython xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse (C _elementtree XMLParser/TreeBuilder) / pyexpat / Expat 2.10.0
family_note: Not an independent XML engine. XMLResource(BytesIO(data)) opens the stream in memory and XMLResourceLoader._parse consumes xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse(fp, ('start-ns', 'end-ns', 'start', 'comment', 'pi', 'end')): CPython's pure-Python iterparse/XMLPullParser driver feeds the C _elementtree XMLParser, which drives pyexpat and Expat 2.10.0 (tokenizing, well-formedness and {uri}local name expansion) and builds the tree with the C TreeBuilder. xmlschema's own parse-time code is the source-type dispatch, the event loop with depth and element limits, and a namespace-map stack plus per-element declaration lists built from start-ns/end-ns events. It shares the Expat family with xmltodict, untangle, defusedxml and the standard xml.etree.ElementTree path (same Expat 2.10.0 pin).
namespace_caveat: XMLResource records xmlns declarations itself from iterparse start-ns events (get_xmlns) and keeps a per-element in-scope namespace map (get_nsmap). The summary's namespace_declarations and namespaces fields come from get_xmlns, a public method with a docstring that is not listed on the Sphinx API page; the documented get_namespaces() merges declarations into one prefix map and cannot give a per-element count. Both controls match the lxml path's full summary, including the declaration count.
parser_options_caveat: Defaults only: defuse='remote' does not pre-scan a BytesIO source with xmlschema's SafeExpatParser, allow='all' and block=None do not apply because a BytesIO source is not a URL, lazy=False builds the full tree, and the MAX_XML_DEPTH=1000 and MAX_XML_ELEMENTS=1,000,000 limits are not reached. Raw bytes are not passed: XMLResource treats a bytes source without a newline that does not start with '<' as a URL or file path, so the harness wraps the input in BytesIO. No DTD, entity, security, limit or malformed-input behavior was tested.

The pinned image asserts the default iterparse, the C XMLParser and TreeBuilder, and pyexpat.EXPAT_VERSION; the feedback check also asserts that the BytesIO source has no URL or file object and is neither defused nor lazy. Both shared valid namespace controls match the lxml path's full summary, including the xmlns declaration count, and an independent lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 oracle run in the verified lxml image; xmlschema's per-element in-scope namespace maps equal lxml's nsmap on every element (including the xmlns="" undeclaration on <plain>), and the URIs of the documented get_namespaces(root_only=False) equal the declared non-empty URIs. name: untangle
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/untangle/1.3.1/json (License-Expression: MIT in wheel METADATA and sdist pyproject.toml; the untangle module docstring says 'License: MIT License'). Neither the wheel nor the sdist ships a separate license file.
input_api: untangle.parse(pathlib.Path(local XML file)); Element._name, _attributes, cdata and children filled by untangle.Handler from SAX startElement/characters/endElement events
documentation_evidence: The official docs say the parse() parameter can be a string, a filename or a URL, and that 'Path-like objects are read as filesystem paths'; the Limitations section documents that untangle substitutes '-', '.' and ':' with '_' in element names. Bytes input is not documented.

dependencies.role: exact Requires-Dist pin; supplies make_parser() -> DefusedExpatParser
C XML parser loaded by CPython pyexpat, built from source

scope: Valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 local files without DOCTYPE through untangle.parse(path-like): raw qualified element names with '-', '.' and ':' replaced by '_' (keywords get a trailing '_'), raw qualified attribute names and values in source order, xmlns/xmlns:* declarations kept as ordinary attributes, per-element concatenated character data (CDATA included), and tree depth. untangle runs the SAX parser with namespace processing off, so it never resolves namespace URIs: element and attribute names carry only the source prefix, and declared URIs appear only as xmlns attribute values. Passing feature_namespaces=True yields an empty tree because untangle.Handler implements startElement but not startElementNS. Comments and processing instructions are not delivered to the handler, and text from mixed content is concatenated per element rather than kept in document order.
family: untangle SAX handler over defusedxml DefusedExpatParser over CPython xml.sax/pyexpat over Expat 2.10.0
family_note: Not an independent XML tokenizer. untangle.parse() calls defusedxml.sax.make_parser(), which returns a DefusedExpatParser (a subclass of CPython's xml.sax.expatreader.ExpatParser that only adds DTD/entity/external-reference guards); pyexpat drives Expat, and untangle.Handler builds its Element tree from startElement/characters/endElement. It shares the Expat family with xmltodict and xml.etree.ElementTree (same Expat 2.10.0 pin).
namespace_caveat: untangle drops namespace URIs. The adapter does not reconstruct them: element names are lossy (':' becomes '_', indistinguishable from '-', '.' or a literal '_'), so any URI in the summary would be adapter-side namespace processing, not untangle's parse result. Shared fields are therefore compared against the independent lxml/libxml2 oracle projected to untangle's documented naming rule, and the expanded names it loses are recorded in data/python/xml/untangle-valid-feedback.json.
parser_options_caveat: defusedxml's DefusedExpatParser defaults are forbid_dtd=False, forbid_entities=True, forbid_external=True; untangle passes no SAX features here. No DTD, entity or malformed-input behavior was tested.
